skill.description: Build Starknet applications with starknet.js v9.x guidance for providers, accounts, contracts, transactions, fees, wallets, and paymasters.

security_audit.summary: All 98 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, normal SDK documentation, explicit service endpoints, or local signing configuration. Two semantic hardening issues remain: the connectivity example needlessly loads a private key and does not enforce an expected Starknet chain ID. No prompt injection, hidden command execution, or secret exfiltration evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Connectivity example creates a signing account for a read-only chain-ID request.
remediation.suggestion: Use RpcProvider alone for connectivity checks. Load a private key and create Account only immediately before an explicit signing operation.

remediation.issue: RPC endpoint is accepted without checking its intended Starknet network.
remediation.suggestion: Compare getChainId() with a caller-selected expected chain ID and stop on mismatch before any signing or transaction flow.

remediation.issue: Transaction examples can be copied into value-moving flows without explicit policy checks.
remediation.suggestion: Document allowlisted contracts, spend limits, simulated results, and user confirmation before approvals, executions, or paymaster requests.

semantic_findings.title: Unnecessary private key use in connectivity example
semantic_findings.description: The connectivity example loads a private key and creates an Account before making only a provider getChainId call. This expands secret exposure without a signing requirement.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The shown code reads STARKNET_PRIVATE_KEY and constructs Account, while the sole network operation is provider.getChainId. A read-only provider is sufficient.

semantic_findings.title: RPC endpoint lacks expected-chain validation
semantic_findings.description: The example accepts any STARKNET_RPC_URL and reports its chain ID without enforcing an expected network. Reusing this pattern for transactions can direct signing workflows to an unintended network.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The RPC URL is environment-controlled and the returned chain ID is only logged. No comparison to an expected chain is present.

content.user_title: Build secure Starknet apps with starknet.js
content.value_statement: Starknet application code needs correct account, provider, fee, and transaction handling. This reference gives focused starknet.js v9.x patterns with security guidance for common workflows.
actual_capabilities: Configure RPC providers for Starknet mainnet and Sepolia.
Create Starknet accounts and manage signing keys in TypeScript.
Read contract state and prepare typed contract calls.
Estimate fees, submit transactions, and wait for receipts.
Integrate wallets, multicalls, paymasters, and token standards.
limitations: Targets starknet.js v9.x and may not match older SDK versions.
Does not deploy contracts or replace a security audit.
Cannot protect keys or approve transactions without user-controlled safeguards.
Endpoint availability and fee behavior depend on external Starknet services.

use_cases.title: Build a contract client
use_cases.description: Create typed reads and writes for a deployed Starknet contract.

use_cases.title: Add wallet transaction flows
use_cases.description: Prepare, estimate, submit, and track user-approved Starknet transactions.

use_cases.title: Review provider configuration
use_cases.description: Set explicit RPC endpoints, chain checks, and fee policies for production.

prompt_templates.title: Start with a provider
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a minimal starknet.js v9.x TypeScript provider setup for Sepolia. Explain each required value and avoid private keys.

prompt_templates.title: Read contract state
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me call a read-only function on this Starknet contract with starknet.js. Ask for ABI, address, function name, and arguments first.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare safe transaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Starknet transaction flow with fee estimation, expected chain validation, contract allowlisting, simulation, and explicit user confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate sponsored execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a starknet.js paymaster integration. Include trusted endpoint configuration, policy validation, failure handling, and receipt monitoring.

output_examples.input: Set up a read-only Starknet provider for Sepolia.
output: Provider configuration using an explicit Sepolia RPC URL.
Expected chain ID validation before contract reads.
Clear guidance that no signer or private key is needed.
Fee estimate and transaction review steps.
Receipt monitoring and error recovery steps.

best_practices: Validate expected chain ID before signing or submitting transactions.
Use a read-only provider unless a workflow must sign.
Simulate transactions and require explicit confirmation for value-moving actions.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode private keys, RPC credentials, or production addresses.
Do not submit transactions without checking contract, calldata, fee, and network.
Do not treat generated random addresses as private keys.

faq.question: Which starknet.js version does this cover?
faq.answer: It covers starknet.js v9.x patterns documented by this skill.

faq.question: Do I need a private key for provider reads?
faq.answer: No. Use RpcProvider for read-only calls and connectivity checks.

faq.question: Can this skill submit transactions?
faq.answer: It provides patterns for preparing and submitting transactions. You must control keys and confirm each value-moving action.

faq.question: How should I select an RPC endpoint?
faq.answer: Use an explicit trusted endpoint per environment and validate the returned chain ID.

faq.question: Does it support paymasters?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents paymaster configuration and sponsored execution patterns.

faq.question: Does it audit my smart contract?
faq.answer: No. It is SDK guidance and does not replace contract, infrastructure, or wallet security review.
